newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPC sells 66 mln new shares to Korea group.
newsitem.headline: IPC sells 66 mln new shares to Korea group.

text.p: IPC Corp said on Tuesday it has entered into a subscription agreement to sell 66 million new shares to the Sungwoo Group of Korea at Singapore $0.60 each for a total of S$39.6 million.
Computer firm IPC said in a statement the sales proceeds would be used to finance the working capital requirements of the group's investments in the telecommunications business.
Sungwoo would manufacture cellular phones currently produced by Hagenuk Telecom GmbH and distribute Hagenuk telecommunications equipment in Korea.
Sungwoo would also distribute IPC group products in Korea and source components in Korea for IPC.

IPC said the issue of the new shares would increase the group's net asset backing per share by 4.03 cents to 32.78 cents, based on the accounts of the group as of June 30, 1996, after adjusting for issue of 33.2 million new shares in January 1997 for a 29 percent stake in Hagenuk.
The Sung group comprises Hyundai Cement Co Ltd and nine other companies.
